"Billion" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of its unclaimed prize money, about three-quarters is in wins under $5,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

How far "Billion" is through its run does not decide anything by itself. It changes how closely to look at the other numbers.

The numbers for "Billion" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
762.headline: Where the prize money is

827.body:
The top prize count on "50th Anniversary" has not moved for over a month. The game still has one of three top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

Every line of 50th Anniversary's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
827.headline: No top prize claimed lately

847.body:
All the top prizes on "Bingo 50X" have been claimed. That lowers the biggest prize from $500,000 to $100,000. That level still has two unclaimed. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

The numbers for "Bingo 50X" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
847.headline: No top prizes remain

891.body:
The most common win left on "Cash Explosion 25X" is $5. The second biggest prize left is $10,000, and one of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

If "Cash Explosion 25X" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
891.headline: What the prize table shows
